title: Continuous Subarray Sum
statement: Return True if some contiguous subarray of length at least 2 has a sum that is a multiple of k (0 counts as a multiple). Values are non-negative and k >= 1.

hints.1_question: Two prefix sums with the same remainder mod k mean the numbers between them sum to a multiple of k. What extra condition does the problem add?
hints.2_nudge: Store, for each remainder, the first index where it appeared. A repeat is valid only if the two positions are at least 2 apart.
hints.3_big_hint: seen = {0: -1}; for i, x: total = (total + x) % k; if total in seen: if i - seen[total] >= 2 return True; else seen[total] = i. Never overwrite the first index.

known_bugs.name: accepts subarrays of length 1
known_bugs.followup: The subarray needs at least two elements. How far apart must the two matching prefixes be?

known_bugs.name: overwrites the first index of a remainder
known_bugs.followup: If the same remainder shows up three times in a row, which earlier index gives you the widest subarray? Are you keeping it?

known_bugs.name: checks every subarray (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many (i, j) pairs does this try when no subarray matches? Which dictionary lookup replaces the inner loop?

followups: Why do you only need the earliest index per remainder?
What changes if k can be 0?
